title: Types of Psychological Tests
summary: Classification of tests by purpose: intelligence, aptitude, achievement, personality, interest, attitude, neuropsychological; speed vs power tests; individual vs group tests.
revision: Tests classified by purpose (intelligence, aptitude, achievement, personality, attitude, interest, neuropsychological), speed vs power, individual vs group.
traps: Achievement measures what has been learned; aptitude measures potential to learn.
Individual tests are one-on-one; group tests are simultaneous.
confusions: Believing all tests are speed tests.

notes.c: Types of psychological tests by purpose

i: Speed test: performance depends on how quickly items are answered; time limit is strict.
Power test: performance depends on item difficulty; ample time is given.
Individual test: administered to one person at a time (e.g., Stanford-Binet).
Group test: administered to many people simultaneously (e.g., group achievement test).

notes.t: UGC NET frequently asks to classify a test by purpose, speed/power, or individual/group administration.

mnemonics.title: IAAPAIN
mnemonics.text: I — Intelligence, A — Aptitude, A — Achievement, P — Personality, A — Attitude, I — Interest, N — Neuropsychological

flashcards.a: Speed test = quick responses under time limit; power test = difficult items with ample time.
